'''Martin Klazar''' (born 1966) is a Czech mathematician specializing in [[enumerative combinatorics]] and [[extremal combinatorics]]. He is a docent (associate professor) in the Department of Applied Mathematics at [[Charles University]] in Prague.<ref>{{cite web |title=Charles University, Department of Applied Mathematics – People |url=https://www.mff.cuni.cz/en/faculty/organizational-structure/people?hdl=603 |access-date=2025-06-19}}</ref> Klazar is known for his work on pattern avoidance in discrete structures (such as permutations and set partitions) and on extremal problems for sequences and matrices.

== Education and career ==
Klazar was born in [[Děčín]], Czechoslovakia (now the Czech Republic) in 1966.<ref>{{Cite web |orig-date=August 2004 |title=Short CV |url=https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~klazar/cv.html |access-date=2025-06-19 |website=kam.mff.cuni.cz}}</ref> He studied mathematics at the [[Charles University]] in [[Prague]] from 1984 to 1989, earning the degree of RNDr. (Rerum Naturalium Doctor). He received his Ph.D. from Charles University in 1995 under the supervision of [[Jaroslav Nešetřil]], with a dissertation on combinatorial aspects of [[Davenport–Schinzel sequence]]s.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Martin Klazar - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=96147 |access-date=2025-06-19 |website=mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> In 1997–98, Klazar was awarded a [[Humboldt Research Fellowship]] to conduct research at the [[University of Bonn]] in Germany under host [[Bernhard Korte]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Martin Klazar |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/connect/explore-the-humboldt-network/singleview/1051363/dr-martin-klazar |access-date=2025-06-19 |website=www.humboldt-foundation.de}}</ref> He later habilitated at Charles University, where he became a docent (associate professor) in the Department of Applied Mathematics.<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
Klazar's research deals with problems in enumerative combinatorics, permutation patterns, and extremal combinatorics.

In a 1992 paper, he proved a general upper bound in the extremal theory of sequences, showing that the maximum length of sequences over an ''n''-letter alphabet in which any two occurrences of the same letter are separated by at least ''k-1'' other letters, and which avoid a fixed forbidden subsequence <math>u</math> of length <math>|u|>4</math> over a ''k''-letter alphabet is almost linear in ''n'' (more precisely, it is <math>O(n2^{O(\alpha(n)^{|u|-4})})</math>, where <math>\alpha(n)</math> denotes the inverse Ackermann function and <math>|u|</math> is the length of <math>u</math>).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Klazar |first=Martin |date=1992 |title=A general upper bound in extremal theory of sequences |url=https://eudml.org/doc/247383 |journal=Commentationes Mathematicae Universitatis Carolinae |volume=33 |issue=4 |pages=737–746 |issn=0010-2628}}</ref>

His 1996 paper "''On <math>abab</math>-free and <math>abba</math>-free set partitions''"<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Klazar |first=Martin |date=1996 |title=On abab-free and abba-free Set Partitions |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0195669896900050 |journal=European Journal of Combinatorics|volume=17 |issue=1 |pages=53–68 |doi=10.1006/eujc.1996.0005|url-access=subscription }}</ref> is credited as initiating<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gunby |first1=Benjamin |last2=Pálvölgyi |first2=Dömötör |date=2019 |title=Asymptotics of pattern avoidance in the Klazar set partition and permutation-tuple settings |journal=European Journal of Combinatorics|volume=82 |pages=Article 102992, 21 pp |article-number=102992 |doi=10.1016/j.ejc.2019.07.003|doi-access=free |arxiv=1707.07809 }}</ref> the study of pattern-avoiding set partitions (analogous to pattern avoidance in permutations), generalizing Germain Kreweras's notion of [[Noncrossing partition|noncrossing partitions]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kreweras |first=G. |date=1972 |title=Sur les partitions non croisees d'un cycle |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0012365X72900416 |journal=Discrete Mathematics |language=fr |volume=1 |issue=4 |pages=333–350 |doi=10.1016/0012-365X(72)90041-6|url-access=subscription }}</ref> That work found connections to [[Davenport–Schinzel sequence]]s and provided exact formulas for the number of set partitions avoiding certain 4-element patterns. Klazar later continued his investigations of pattern-avoiding set partitions in other works.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Klazar |first=Martin |date=2000 |title=Counting pattern-free set partitions I: A generalization of Stirling numbers of the second kind |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0195669899903530 |journal=European Journal of Combinatorics|volume=21 |issue=3 |pages=367–378 |doi=10.1006/eujc.1999.0353|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Klazar |first=Martin |date=2000 |title=Counting pattern-free set partitions II: Noncrossing and other hypergraphs |url=https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/v7i1r34 |journal=The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics |volume=7 |issue=1 |pages=25 pp |doi=10.37236/1512 |issn=1077-8926}}</ref>

In 2000, Klazar showed that the long-standing [[Stanley–Wilf conjecture]] on permutation patterns would follow from an extremal conjecture of Zoltán Füredi and Péter Hajnal concerning forbidden submatrices.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Klazar |first=Martin |chapter=The Füredi-Hajnal Conjecture Implies the Stanley-Wilf Conjecture |date=2000 |editor-last=Krob |editor-first=Daniel |editor2-last=Mikhalev |editor2-first=Alexander A. |editor3-last=Mikhalev |editor3-first=Alexander V. |title=Formal Power Series and Algebraic Combinatorics |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-662-04166-6_22 |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |pages=250–255 |doi=10.1007/978-3-662-04166-6_22 |isbn=978-3-662-04166-6|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref> This approach foreshadowed the subsequent 2004 proof of the Stanley–Wilf conjecture by [[Adam Marcus (mathematician)|Adam Marcus]] and [[Gábor Tardos]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Marcus |first1=Adam |last2=Tardos |first2=Gábor |date=2004 |title=Excluded permutation matrices and the Stanley–Wilf conjecture |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0097316504000512 |journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A|volume=107 |issue=1 |pages=153–160 |doi=10.1016/j.jcta.2004.04.002|url-access=subscription }}</ref> for which Marcus was awarded the inaugural [[Dénes König Prize]] in 2008.

Klazar's joint 2002 paper with Tomáš Kaiser, "''On growth rates of closed permutation classes"'' was the first research to systemically consider the set of possible [[Stanley–Wilf conjecture#Allowable growth rates|growth rates of permutation classes]]. Their paper characterized all accumulation points of growth constants below 2, showing in particular that 2 is the least accumulation point of permutation class growth rates, and that there are no such growth rates between 1 and the [[golden ratio]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kaiser |first1=Tomáš |last2=Klazar |first2=Martin |date=2003 |title=On growth rates of closed permutation classes |url=https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/v9i2r10 |journal=The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics |volume=9 |issue=2 |pages=20 pp |doi=10.37236/1682 |issn=1077-8926|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
